title: Comprehensions
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Comprehensions in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: List comprehension
items.text: A list comprehension creates a list from an expression and an iteration in a compact form.

items.heading: Comprehension structure
items.text: The basic form is [expression for item in iterable].

items.heading: Condition in comprehension
items.text: An if condition can filter which items are included.
items.code: [x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]

items.heading: Dict comprehension
items.text: A dictionary comprehension creates key-value pairs in a dictionary.

items.heading: Set comprehension
items.text: A set comprehension creates a set of computed values.

items.heading: range() with comprehension
items.text: range() is often used when a comprehension needs a sequence of numbers.

items.heading: Calling functions
items.text: The expression part of a comprehension can call a function.

items.heading: Readable code
items.text: Comprehensions are useful when the logic is simple. Very complex comprehensions are harder to read than normal loops.

items.heading: Normal loop alternative
items.text: A normal for loop is often better when there are many steps or nested conditions.

items.heading: Result type
items.text: The brackets used by the comprehension determine its result type: [] for list, {} with key:value for dict, and {} with an expression for set.
